summary: BC Geographical Names marks Hicks Hill as the site of the Hicks Hill (wildfire) Lookout; no build, staffing or fate source was reached.

evidence.supports: The hill is the location of the Hicks Hill (wildfire) Lookout.
evidence.quote: Origin/significance not recorded - this is the location of Hicks Hill (wildfire) Lookout.

evidence.supports: The hill lies west of the junction of Tchesinkut Creek and the Endako River, between Fraser Lake and Burns Lake.
evidence.quote: W of junction of Tchesinkut Creek and Endako River, between Fraser Lake and Burns Lake (communities)

evidence.supports: The place name was adopted on 19 January 1961.
The site is in the Bulkley-Nechako area.

notes_for_editor: Very thin record. No fetched page gives a build date, builder, staffing, access rule or current condition. A Facebook group post titled 'Saturday Double Feature - Hicks Lookout and Sinkut Lookout' (seen only as a search snippet; both fetch_text and WebFetch returned only its title) says the Hicks Hill lookout was built in 1949 with a BC Archives photo from 1951, and describes 4x4 access and condition. That text is not used because no fetched page carried it; check it by hand before adding a build date. The BC Archives record 'Forest Service Priestly Hill Lookout' (search-bcarchives.royalbcmuseum.bc.ca) failed to load in both tools (certificate error), and may hold the build date. The 1961 date is the place-name adoption, not the tower. The Canada Lookouts page lists elevation 853 with no unit; not used. The story is about 70 words, below the 120-word floor, because the sources do not support more. Recommend holding it until the BC Archives record can be read. Fact-check 2026-10-20: all four claims are on the cited pages and none was removed; the one sentence that copied quote wording was reworded. Read budget was exceeded: about eight page reads and two WebFetch calls for this tower, and no WebSearch beyond the two allowed.
